VIDEO.title: The REAL Message of the Transfiguration Everyone Missed
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

hand: His face shone like the sun.
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 17:1-13. Six days later Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and He is transfigured: His face shines like the sun and His garments become white as light. Moses and Elijah appear, talking with Him. Peter offers to make three booths; a bright cloud overshadows them and a voice says, 'This is My beloved Son, with whom I am well-pleased; listen to Him!' Coming down, the disciples ask why the scribes say Elijah must come first, and Jesus points to John the Baptist.

The light comes from the inside out, first His face, then His clothes (Mark 9:3; Luke 9:29). Luke says Moses and Elijah spoke of His departure, in Greek His exodus (Luke 9:31): the new Moses will lead a new exodus through His death and resurrection. No one knows which mountain; many say Tabor, the video favors Hermon.

Moses and Elijah both met God on a mountain (Exodus 19; 24; 1 Kings 19), and Moses' face shone (Exodus 34:29-30). But Moses reflected glory from outside; Jesus is 'the radiance of His glory' (Hebrews 1:3). Moses and Elijah stand for the Law and the Prophets (5:17) and are also types of Christ, as D. A. Carson notes.

Every element recalls Sinai: a mountain after six days, three witnesses, shining glory, the cloud, and then a tabernacle, which is what Peter suggests. The Father's words gather Psalm 2:7, Isaiah 42:1 and Deuteronomy 18:15, one text from each part of the Tanakh.

The disciples' question about Elijah (Malachi 4:5-6) shows a flawed view of the day of the Lord. Hearts must be turned first, a work of God's Spirit (Ezekiel 36). The lesson: the restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of His people to God.
QUOTES: The metamorphosis of Jesus did not come from the outside in, but from the inside out.
The restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of his people to God.
God quotes the Tanakh in order to testify to the disciples who Jesus is. That's no accident, friends.
The restoration of the world is first accomplished by the restoration of people's hearts to God.

LSB_QUOTES.text: And He was transfigured before them; and His face shone like the sun, and His garments became as white as light.
While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, with whom I am well-pleased; listen to Him!”
And he will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land, devoting it to destruction.”

src.text: And He was transfigured before them; and His face shone like the sun, and His garments became as white as light.

lines.text: The shining starts from Jesus' face and then extends to His clothes. Mark: 'as no launderer on earth can whiten them' (Mark 9:3). Luke: 'His clothing became white and gleaming' (Luke 9:29).
Those who know the end of the Gospels cannot help but think of the morning of the third day when the stone was rolled away.

src.text: And behold, two men were talking with Him, and they were Moses and Elijah, who, appearing in glory, were speaking of His departure which He was about to fulfill at Jerusalem.

lines.text: In Greek, 'departure' is exodos. Jesus is the new Moses who leads God's people into a new exodus, not by marching into the desert but by dying and rising, with the gathering of His people afterward.
Mark says the disciples argued about 'what rising from the dead meant' (Mark 9:10). The whole scene helps them wrestle with His death, resurrection and ascension.

left.text: Now it happened when Moses was coming down from Mount Sinai (and the two tablets of the testimony were in Moses’ hand as he was coming down from the mountain), that Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because of his speaking with Him.

right.text: who is the radiance of His glory and the exact representation of His nature, and upholds all things by the word of His power; who, having accomplished cleansing for sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,

lines.text: Moses' face shone because God's glory was transmitted to him from outside. Jesus' light comes from inside Him.
Why so bright? Because the glory of the Lord is shown as a very bright light (Psalm 43:3; Isaiah 60:1; Revelation 21:23).

left.text: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Him.

right.text: “Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.

lines.text: Moses stands for the Law and Elijah for the Prophets, a picture of what Jesus said about fulfilling them (5:17).

They are also types of Christ. The video cites D. A. Carson: both men met God's glory on a mountain (Sinai and Horeb) and both suffered rejection, so Jesus, clearly superior to them, will walk a path that parallels theirs.

left.text: And the glory of Yahweh dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days; and on the seventh day He called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.

right.text: And six days later Jesus *brought with Him Peter and James and John his brother, and *led them up on a high mountain by themselves.

lines.text: Jesus takes His disciples up a mountain to meet the Lord, as Moses went up to God (Exodus 19:3) and Elijah stood on the mountain before Yahweh (1 Kings 19:11).
Six days recalls God calling Moses up Sinai.

src.text: Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,

lines.text: Peter, James and John are witnesses, as Aaron, Nadab and Abihu went up with Moses.

Seventy elders went too, and Joshua went further up with Moses (Exodus 24:13). Peter later writes, 'we ourselves heard this utterance made from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain' (2 Peter 1:18).

left.text: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You wish, I will make three booths here, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

right.text: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.

lines.text: God speaks out of a cloud, the Shekinah cloud. Anyone who knew Exodus 24 would know what came next after Sinai: the tabernacle. That is exactly what Peter suggests.
Mark: 'For he did not know what to answer; for they became terrified' (Mark 9:6).

src.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, with whom I am well-pleased; listen to Him!”

lines.text: 'My beloved Son' echoes Psalm 2:7, from the Writings (Ketuvim). 'Well-pleased' echoes Isaiah 42:1, from the Prophets (Nevi'im). 'Listen to Him' echoes Deuteronomy 18:15, from the Torah.
God quotes the whole Tanakh to testify who Jesus is. The video adds that Jewish midrash taught the Messiah would be confirmed by all three parts.

left.text: And His disciples asked Him, saying, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

right.text: “Behold, I am going to send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of Yahweh.

lines.text: The disciples walk down the mountain thinking about Malachi 4:5-6. Their question seems to come from confusion: Jesus keeps speaking of suffering.

MALACHI.title: A day of judgment and salvation

src.text: Behold, the day of Yahweh is coming, / Cruel, with fury and burning anger, / To make the land a desolation; / And He will exterminate its sinners from it.

lines.text: The disciples probably held a flawed or incomplete view of the day of the Lord, a theme taught throughout the Old Testament (Isaiah 13; Zechariah 14:1-5; Ezekiel 13:5; Zephaniah 1). It is a day of God's judgment and also His salvation.

left.text: And he will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land, devoting it to destruction.”

right.text: Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.

lines.text: Returning to God's ways can only be a work of God through His Spirit. Jesus alluded to Ezekiel 36 when He told Nicodemus about being born of water and spirit (John 3).
The disciples had no concept of God dealing with sin by putting it on Christ on the cross, yet that had to come before the restoration of the world.

src.text: but I say to you that Elijah already came, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands.” Then the disciples understood that He had spoken to them about John the Baptist.

lines.text: The restoration of the world is first accomplished by the restoration of people's hearts to God, through Jesus' rejection, death and resurrection. So the lesson: the restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of His people to God.
The disciples got it later: see how Peter explains Pentecost (Acts 2) and how Paul describes the end in 1 Corinthians 15.

TERMS.def: Jesus' change of form on the mountain (Greek metamorphoō).
Luke's word for what Moses and Elijah discussed (Luke 9:31): His death, resurrection and ascension as a new exodus.
A later Jewish word for God's dwelling presence, often pictured in the cloud. The captions write 'Shikina.'
The Hebrew Bible: Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets), Ketuvim (Writings). The captions write 'Neim' and 'Ketuim.'
Jewish interpretation of Scripture. The captions write 'Midash.'
Yom Adonai: God's day of judgment and salvation.
A person or event that foreshadows Christ, as Moses and Elijah do.

WORDS.gloss: To transform, change form. Look up: BDAG, μεταμορφόω.
Departure, exit; used of death. The Greek name of the book of Exodus.
To overshadow; used of the Spirit at Jesus' conception (Luke 1:35).
To restore, put back in order.
To shine, send out rays; related to qeren, horn. Look up: BDB or HALOT, קרן.

BACKGROUND.p: Origen and Cyril of Jerusalem name Mount Tabor, and churches have stood on its summit since the Byzantine period. Many modern scholars prefer Hermon because the Gospels call it 'a high mountain' and the last place named is Caesarea Philippi; some suggest Mount Meron. The Gospels do not say.

Shekinah, from the Hebrew for 'to dwell,' is a word of the later rabbis for God's presence among His people. The Bible itself speaks of the cloud and the glory filling the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34) and the temple (1 Kings 8:10-11).
Malachi 4:5-6 closes the Prophets in the Christian Old Testament. Jewish tradition still leaves a cup for Elijah at Passover, and the Mishnah expects him to settle disputes (Mishnah Eduyot 8:7).

DEBATES.p: Tradition since the fourth century says Tabor; the 'high mountain' and the setting near Caesarea Philippi lead many to Hermon. A Roman-era settlement on Tabor's top makes some doubt the privacy of 'by themselves.'
Jesus says both 'Elijah is coming' (17:11) and 'Elijah already came' (17:12). Some see John as the full fulfillment; others expect a further coming before the end (Revelation 11:3-6 is often cited).
Readers have seen the Law and the Prophets, two men who met God on Sinai/Horeb, two whose departures were unusual, or (Chrysostom) servants placed beside the Lord to show the difference.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The quote given as 'Exodus 19:2' runs on into 19:3; 'Moses went up to God, and Yahweh called to him from the mountain' is verse 3.
1 Kings 19 says Yahweh 'was not in the wind' but came in 'a sound of a thin gentle whisper' (1 Kings 19:11-12). Elijah went up 'by a whirlwind' in 2 Kings 2:11.
'Isaiah 13:16' should be 13:6 or 13:9, where the day of Yahweh is named.
Mount Tabor lies in Lower Galilee, not south of Galilee.
Exodus 24 has Aaron, Nadab and Abihu and also seventy elders and Joshua, so the three witnesses are not alone.

The claim that midrash taught the Messiah would be confirmed by all three parts of the Tanakh is not sourced in the video, and the D. A. Carson quotation could not be checked here; it is summarized, not quoted.
The captions write 'Tabore' and 'Hermmon,' 'Shikina' for Shekinah, 'Ketuim' and 'Neim' for Ketuvim and Nevi'im, 'Midash' for midrash, and 'Abihoo' for Abihu.

QUESTIONS: What difference does it make that Jesus' glory shines from within rather than being reflected?
Why do you think Moses and Elijah talked with Him about His 'departure'?
Peter wanted to build booths and stay. When do you try to hold onto a mountaintop moment?
'Listen to Him!' What is Jesus saying to you that you would rather not hear?
How does the day of the Lord bring both judgment and salvation?
Where do you need God to turn your heart before anything else can be restored?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson, stated plainly: the restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of His people to God. The disciples were confused because they had not wrestled with God's requirement to turn the hearts of His people back to Him, and they had no concept of God dealing with sin by putting it on Christ on the cross. Yet that was necessary before the restoration of the world. In other words, the restoration of the world is first accomplished by the restoration of people's hearts to God, and that is accomplished through the rejection, the death and the resurrection of Jesus. The disciples learned it, as Peter's sermon at Pentecost and Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians 15 show, and there are lots of implications that still affect us today.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): read Matthew 17:5 aloud and finish the sentence, 'This week I will listen to Him about…' Then pray Ezekiel 36:26 for one person whose heart you long to see turned to God.

## A new Sinai
1. Exodus 24:15-16; Matthew 17:1: A mountain, after six days
   Exodus (Exodus 24:16, LSB): "And the glory of Yahweh dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days; and on the seventh day He called to Moses from the midst of the cloud."
   Matthew (Matthew 17:1, LSB): "And six days later Jesus *brought with Him Peter and James and John his brother, and *led them up on a high mountain by themselves."
   (video) Jesus takes His disciples up a mountain to meet the Lord, as Moses went up to God (Exodus 19:3) and Elijah stood on the mountain before Yahweh (1 Kings 19:11). (Exodus 19:3; 1 Kings 19:11)
   (video) Six days recalls God calling Moses up Sinai.
2. Exodus 24:1, 9: Three witnesses
   Witnesses Exodus 24:9: "Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel," https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Exodus+24:9
   (video) Peter, James and John are witnesses, as Aaron, Nadab and Abihu went up with Moses.
   [Background] Seventy elders went too, and Joshua went further up with Moses (Exodus 24:13). Peter later writes, 'we ourselves heard this utterance made from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain' (2 Peter 1:18). (Exodus 24:13; 2 Peter 1:18)
3. Matthew 17:4-5; Exodus 40:34: The cloud and the booths
   Peter (Matthew 17:4, LSB): "And Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You wish, I will make three booths here, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”"
   Exodus (Exodus 40:34, LSB): "Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle."
   (video) God speaks out of a cloud, the Shekinah cloud. Anyone who knew Exodus 24 would know what came next after Sinai: the tabernacle. That is exactly what Peter suggests.
   [Background] Mark: 'For he did not know what to answer; for they became terrified' (Mark 9:6). (Mark 9:6)
4. Matthew 17:5: Torah, Prophets and Writings
   Tanakh Matthew 17:5: "While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, with whom I am well-pleased; listen to Him!”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+17:5
   (video) 'My beloved Son' echoes Psalm 2:7, from the Writings (Ketuvim). 'Well-pleased' echoes Isaiah 42:1, from the Prophets (Nevi'im). 'Listen to Him' echoes Deuteronomy 18:15, from the Torah. (Psalms 2:7; Isaiah 42:1; Deuteronomy 18:15)
   (video) God quotes the whole Tanakh to testify who Jesus is. The video adds that Jewish midrash taught the Messiah would be confirmed by all three parts.

## Elijah must come first
1. Matthew 17:10-11; Malachi 4:5: Elijah must come first
   The disciples (Matthew 17:10, LSB): "And His disciples asked Him, saying, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”"
   Malachi (Malachi 4:5, LSB): "“Behold, I am going to send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of Yahweh."
   (video) The disciples walk down the mountain thinking about Malachi 4:5-6. Their question seems to come from confusion: Jesus keeps speaking of suffering.
2. Day of the Lord: A day of judgment and salvation
   Yom Adonai Isaiah 13:9: "Behold, the day of Yahweh is coming, / Cruel, with fury and burning anger, / To make the land a desolation; / And He will exterminate its sinners from it." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Isaiah+13:9
   (video) The disciples probably held a flawed or incomplete view of the day of the Lord, a theme taught throughout the Old Testament (Isaiah 13; Zechariah 14:1-5; Ezekiel 13:5; Zephaniah 1). It is a day of God's judgment and also His salvation. (Zechariah 14:1-5; Ezekiel 13:5)
3. Malachi 4:6; Ezekiel 36:26-27: Hearts turned by God's Spirit
   Malachi (Malachi 4:6, LSB): "And he will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land, devoting it to destruction.”"
   Ezekiel (Ezekiel 36:26, LSB): "Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh."
   (video) Returning to God's ways can only be a work of God through His Spirit. Jesus alluded to Ezekiel 36 when He told Nicodemus about being born of water and spirit (John 3). (John 3:5)
   (video) The disciples had no concept of God dealing with sin by putting it on Christ on the cross, yet that had to come before the restoration of the world.
4. Matthew 17:12-13: Elijah already came
   Lesson Matthew 17:12-13: "but I say to you that Elijah already came, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands.” Then the disciples understood that He had spoken to them about John the Baptist." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+17:12-13
   (video) The restoration of the world is first accomplished by the restoration of people's hearts to God, through Jesus' rejection, death and resurrection. So the lesson: the restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of His people to God.
   (video) The disciples got it later: see how Peter explains Pentecost (Acts 2) and how Paul describes the end in 1 Corinthians 15. (Acts 2:16-21)

## Key people
- Peter, James and John: The inner circle, witnesses on the mountain like Aaron, Nadab and Abihu. [Background] The same three are with Jesus at Jairus' house and in Gethsemane (Mark 5:37; 14:33).
- Moses: Stands for the Law; met God on Sinai; his face shone. [Background] Deuteronomy 34:6 says no one knows his grave.
- Elijah: Stands for the Prophets; met God on Horeb; expected before the day of Yahweh. [Background] He was taken up 'by a whirlwind to heaven' (2 Kings 2:11).
- John the Baptist: The Elijah who already came. [Background] Jesus said so earlier: 'John himself is Elijah who was to come' (Matthew 11:14).
- The scribes: Taught that Elijah must come first. [Background] Their teaching rests on Malachi 4:5.

## Places [Background]
- Mount Tabor (named in the video): The traditional site of the transfiguration; the captions write 'Tabore.'
- Mount Hermon (named in the video): The high mountain near Caesarea Philippi, which the video favors.
- Caesarea Philippi (named in the video): Where Jesus and the disciples were in 16:13.
- Nazareth: Jesus' hometown, a few miles west of Tabor.

## Key terms
- Transfiguration: Jesus' change of form on the mountain (Greek metamorphoō).
- Exodus (departure): Luke's word for what Moses and Elijah discussed (Luke 9:31): His death, resurrection and ascension as a new exodus.
- Shekinah: A later Jewish word for God's dwelling presence, often pictured in the cloud. The captions write 'Shikina.'
- Tanakh: The Hebrew Bible: Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets), Ketuvim (Writings). The captions write 'Neim' and 'Ketuim.'
- Midrash: Jewish interpretation of Scripture. The captions write 'Midash.'
- Day of the Lord: Yom Adonai: God's day of judgment and salvation.
- Type: A person or event that foreshadows Christ, as Moses and Elijah do.

- ἔξοδος exodos (G1841, Greek): Departure, exit; used of death. The Greek name of the book of Exodus. (Luke 9:31)
- σκηνή skēnē (G4633, Greek): Tent, booth, tabernacle. (Matt 17:4)
- νεφέλη nephelē (G3507, Greek): Cloud. (Matt 17:5)
- ἐπισκιάζω episkiazō (G1982, Greek): To overshadow; used of the Spirit at Jesus' conception (Luke 1:35). (Matt 17:5)
- εὐδοκέω eudokeō (G2106, Greek): To be well-pleased, take delight. (Matt 17:5)
- ἀποκαθίστημι apokathistēmi (G600, Greek): To restore, put back in order. (Matt 17:11)

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Which mountain?: Origen and Cyril of Jerusalem name Mount Tabor, and churches have stood on its summit since the Byzantine period. Many modern scholars prefer Hermon because the Gospels call it 'a high mountain' and the last place named is Caesarea Philippi; some suggest Mount Meron. The Gospels do not say.
- Shekinah: Shekinah, from the Hebrew for 'to dwell,' is a word of the later rabbis for God's presence among His people. The Bible itself speaks of the cloud and the glory filling the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34) and the temple (1 Kings 8:10-11).
- Elijah expected: Malachi 4:5-6 closes the Prophets in the Christian Old Testament. Jewish tradition still leaves a cup for Elijah at Passover, and the Mishnah expects him to settle disputes (Mishnah Eduyot 8:7).

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "He brings the leaders of His choir, that they might see the difference even hereby between the servants and the Lord" Homilies on Matthew 56, on 17:3. Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "To show the glory of the cross, and to console Peter and the others in their dread of the passion, and to raise up their minds." Homilies on Matthew 56, on 17:3. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "For of the first, John was forerunner; whom Christ called also Elias, not because he was Elias, but because he was fulfilling the ministry of that prophet." Homilies on Matthew 57, on 17:10-12. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Tabor or Hermon? Tradition since the fourth century says Tabor; the 'high mountain' and the setting near Caesarea Philippi lead many to Hermon. A Roman-era settlement on Tabor's top makes some doubt the privacy of 'by themselves.'
- Is Elijah still to come? Jesus says both 'Elijah is coming' (17:11) and 'Elijah already came' (17:12). Some see John as the full fulfillment; others expect a further coming before the end (Revelation 11:3-6 is often cited).
- Why Moses and Elijah? Readers have seen the Law and the Prophets, two men who met God on Sinai/Horeb, two whose departures were unusual, or (Chrysostom) servants placed beside the Lord to show the difference.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The quote given as 'Exodus 19:2' runs on into 19:3; 'Moses went up to God, and Yahweh called to him from the mountain' is verse 3.
- 1 Kings 19 says Yahweh 'was not in the wind' but came in 'a sound of a thin gentle whisper' (1 Kings 19:11-12). Elijah went up 'by a whirlwind' in 2 Kings 2:11.
- 'Isaiah 13:16' should be 13:6 or 13:9, where the day of Yahweh is named.
- Mount Tabor lies in Lower Galilee, not south of Galilee.
- Exodus 24 has Aaron, Nadab and Abihu and also seventy elders and Joshua, so the three witnesses are not alone.
- The claim that midrash taught the Messiah would be confirmed by all three parts of the Tanakh is not sourced in the video, and the D. A. Carson quotation could not be checked here; it is summarized, not quoted.
- The captions write 'Tabore' and 'Hermmon,' 'Shikina' for Shekinah, 'Ketuim' and 'Neim' for Ketuvim and Nevi'im, 'Midash' for midrash, and 'Abihoo' for Abihu.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What difference does it make that Jesus' glory shines from within rather than being reflected?
2. Why do you think Moses and Elijah talked with Him about His 'departure'?
3. Peter wanted to build booths and stay. When do you try to hold onto a mountaintop moment?
4. 'Listen to Him!' What is Jesus saying to you that you would rather not hear?
5. How does the day of the Lord bring both judgment and salvation?
6. Where do you need God to turn your heart before anything else can be restored?

## Application
- (video) The lesson, stated plainly: the restoration of the world will be fully complete after Christ turns the hearts of His people to God. The disciples were confused because they had not wrestled with God's requirement to turn the hearts of His people back to Him, and they had no concept of God dealing with sin by putting it on Christ on the cross. Yet that was necessary before the restoration of the world. In other words, the restoration of the world is first accomplished by the restoration of people's hearts to God, and that is accomplished through the rejection, the death and the resurrection of Jesus. The disciples learned it, as Peter's sermon at Pentecost and Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians 15 show, and there are lots of implications that still affect us today.
- Study note (added): read Matthew 17:5 aloud and finish the sentence, 'This week I will listen to Him about…' Then pray Ezekiel 36:26 for one person whose heart you long to see turned to God.
